# --- create a tiny network -------------------------------------------------
net = pp.create_empty_network()

# buses
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
b2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
b3 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)

# external grid
pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=b1, vm_pu=1.02, va_degree=0)

# lines
l1 = pp.create_line_from_parameters(net, from_bus=b1, to_bus=b2,
                                    length_km=1.0, r_ohm_per_km=0.1,
                                    x_ohm_per_km=0.2, c_nf_per_km=10,
                                    max_i_ka=0.4)
l2 = pp.create_line_from_parameters(net, from_bus=b2, to_bus=b3,
                                    length_km=1.0, r_ohm_per_km=0.1,
                                    x_ohm_per_km=0.2, c_nf_per_km=10,
                                    max_i_ka=0.4)

# load
pp.create_load(net, bus=b3, p_mw=0.1, q_mvar=0.05)

# --- control function that can be used with run_timeseries -----------------
def run_control_fct(net):
    """Return loading information for N‑0 and N‑1 (single line outage)."""
    # N‑0 case
    pp.runpp(net)
    base_loading = net.res_line.loading_percent.max()

    # N‑1 case: outage of each line one after the other
    contingencies = [{'element': 'line', 'index': idx} for idx in net.line.index]
    cont_res = pp.run_contingency(net, contingency_list=contingencies)

    # extract loading percent values from all N‑1 results
    max_loading = cont_res['loading_percent'].max()
    min_loading = cont_res['loading_percent'].min()

    return {
        'loading_percent': base_loading,
        'max_loading_percent': max_loading,
        'min_loading_percent': min_loading
    }

# --- run the function and display results ----------------------------------
result = run_control_fct(net)
print("Contingency analysis results:")
print(result)
print("Contingency analysis completed.")

net = pp.create_empty_network()

bus_lv = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=0.4, name="LV Bus")

    pp.runpp(net)                    # power flow
    print(f"t={t}: load p_mw = {net.res_load.p_mw.at[load_idx]:.2f} MW")

print("ConstControl demonstration completed.")

bus_lv = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=0.4)

load_profile = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "p_mw": [0.10, 0.20, 0.15, 0.05],
        "q_mvar": [0.05, 0.10, 0.07, 0.03],
    },
    index=time_steps,
)

# --- controllers that feed the time series into the network ----------------
ConstControl(
    net,
    element="load",
    variable="p_mw",
    element_index=[load_idx],
    data_source=load_profile["p_mw"],
)
ConstControl(
    net,
    element="load",
    variable="q_mvar",
    element_index=[load_idx],
    data_source=load_profile["q_mvar"],
)

# --- set up an OutputWriter (no keyword argument needed) -------------------
output_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
ow = OutputWriter(net, output_path=output_dir, output_file_type="csv")

# --- run the time series simulation ----------------------------------------
ts.run_timeseries(net, time_steps=time_steps)

print(f"Time series simulation finished. Results are stored in: {output_dir}")

    name="Bus voltage (pu)",
    showlegend=True
)

import pandapower as pp
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point, LineString

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create a minimal network with two buses and one line
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
net = pp.create_empty_network()

bus1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20, name="bus1")
bus2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20, name="bus2")

pp.create_line_from_parameters(
    net,
    from_bus=bus1,
    to_bus=bus2,
    length_km=0.1,
    r_ohm_per_km=0.1,
    x_ohm_per_km=0.2,
    c_nf_per_km=10,
    max_i_ka=0.4,
    name="line1",
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Attach simple geodata (WGS84 – EPSG:4326)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
net.bus_geodata = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    geometry=[
        Point(-0.1, 51.5),   # lon, lat for bus1
        Point(-0.12, 51.51), # lon, lat for bus2
    ],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
    index=[bus1, bus2],
)

net.line_geodata = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    geometry=[
        LineString([(-0.1, 51.5), (-0.12, 51.51)]),  # geometry for line1
    ],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
    index=[0],  # line index (only one line)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Convert the CRS from EPSG:4326 (WGS84) to EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
pp.convert_crs(net, epsg_in=4326, epsg_out=3857)

# After CRS conversion, update the internal GIS representations
pp.convert_geodata_to_gis(net)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Simple confirmation output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print("CRS conversion completed.")
print("Bus geodata CRS:", net.bus_geodata.crs)
print("Line geodata CRS:", net.line_geodata.crs)
